live.name: NICKEL HYATT
live.headline: NICKEL HYATT: a threat actor known by many names
live.in_short: NICKEL HYATT is the Secureworks name for an actor also tracked as APT45 and Andariel. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL HYATT is the name Secureworks uses for this threat actor.
It is also tracked under other names, including APT45, Andariel, Dark Seoul, Jumpy Pisces, Onyx Sleet, RIFLE Campaign, Silent Chollima, Stonefly and UN614.
The catalogue lists these tools for the actor: ActiveX 0-day, DTrack, HazyLoad, HotCriossant, Rifle, UnitBot and Valefor.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL HYATT
next.headline: NICKEL HYATT (Andariel): a North Korea-linked group hitting South Korean defense and industry
next.in_short: NICKEL HYATT, also called Andariel or APT45, is tracked by several firms as a North Korea-linked actor. Reports describe attacks on South Korean defense, construction and tech firms, plus ransomware used for money.

sentences.t: NICKEL HYATT is the Secureworks name. The catalogue also lists the aliases APT45, Andariel, Silent Chollima, Onyx Sleet, Stonefly, Jumpy Pisces, Dark Seoul and UN614.

CrowdStrike tracks SILENT CHOLLIMA as a North Korea-nexus adversary active since at least 2007. CrowdStrike assesses it is likely affiliated with Lab 110 within Bureau 3 of the General Reconnaissance Information Bureau.
AhnLab's ASEC says Andariel is either in a cooperative relationship with the Lazarus group or is a subsidiary of it. The report does not say which.

In September 2019, the US Treasury sanctioned three North Korean hacking groups: Lazarus, Andariel and Bluenoroff. Treasury said the aim was to stop stolen funds flowing back to the country's weapons programmes.

ASEC says Andariel usually targets South Korean companies and institutions. Main targets include national defense, political organisations, shipbuilding, energy and telecommunications. Universities, logistics and ICT firms are also hit.

South Korea's National Police Agency said Andariel stole account details from an employee of a maintenance company. It then used the account to install malware on the servers of defense subcontractors.
South Korea's National Cyber Security Center said Andariel hit construction and machinery firms in 2024. The advisory believes the aim was to steal trade secrets.

The US Treasury says Andariel targets South Korea's government and infrastructure to collect information and create disorder. Treasury attributes its intelligence-gathering activity to industry and press reporting.
ASEC says the group has used spear phishing, watering-hole and supply chain attacks. It has also exploited the Log4Shell flaw, targeted poorly managed MS-SQL servers and abused legitimate software.

ASEC reported that Andariel used a malicious file for RID Hijacking. The technique changes an account's identifier so a hidden, low-privilege account is treated as an administrator. ASEC says such an account cannot be completely hidden.
Kudelski Security and Sekoia note that Andariel is unusual among North Korea-linked clusters. It used custom ransomware, Maui and H0lyGh0st, for financial theft.

Since early October 2023, Microsoft has seen Onyx Sleet exploit a TeamCity server flaw, CVE-2023-42793. Onyx Sleet created a new user account and deployed the HazyLoad proxy tool. Microsoft assesses the actor may be compromising vulnerable servers opportunistically.

ASEC analysed Andariel attacks from the first half of 2023. They abused the Innorix Agent file-transfer tool and used Go-based backdoors such as Goat RAT and DurianBeacon. ASEC says the initial distribution route was not confirmed.
In November 2023, ASEC assumed Andariel was exploiting the Apache ActiveMQ flaw CVE-2023-46604 to install NukeSped and TigerRat backdoors. It said it had no direct logs confirming this.

In April 2024, South Korea's police agency warned that Lazarus, Andariel and Kimsuky had breached defense companies and subcontractors. It said some firms had been compromised since late 2022 without knowing it.

South Korea's National Cyber Security Center said Andariel abused a flaw in a domestic VPN's update process in April 2024. It used the flaw to push fake updates that installed the DoraRAT remote access trojan.
Patch internet-facing servers quickly, keep a clear inventory of software and accounts, and keep work and personal passwords separate.
